title: Improving the Distributional Alignment of LLMs using Supervision

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the alignment of LLM-generated opinion distributions with human survey responses across different age groups (e.g., 15-29, 30-49, 50+) by measuring Wasserstein distance between the model's generated probability distributions and actual survey data.

Measuring how accurately LLMs model the opinion distributions of various socioeconomic groups by evaluating model outputs across different income brackets, education levels, and employment statuses against ground-truth survey data.
Comparing the alignment of LLM-elicited opinion distributions with human survey responses from male and female demographic groups on subjective global and societal questions.
Assessing alignment disparities in LLMs when modeling the opinion distributions of respondents from different world regions, US regions, and rural vs. urban living areas.

Evaluating the representational accuracy of LLMs by comparing their generated opinion distributions for different political ideologies (e.g., liberal, conservative) and party affiliations against actual survey responses.
Measuring the alignment of LLM-generated opinion distributions for various racial and ethnic groups using human public opinion survey data as ground truth.

Assessing how well LLMs simulate the opinion distributions of different religious affiliations (e.g., Protestant, Catholic, Muslim, Buddhist, Hindu, Atheist) compared to actual human responses in public opinion and values surveys.
